title: JEE Main 2026 (April 2nd, Shift 2) - Chemistry - Chemical Kinetics
subject: Chemistry

questions.q:
Consider the reaction $aX \rightarrow bY$, for which the rate constant at $30^\circ\text{C}$ is $1 \times 10^{-3}\text{ mol}^{-1}\text{ L s}^{-1}$. Which of the following statements are true?
A. When concentration of 'X' is increased to four times, the rate of reaction becomes 16 times.
B. The reaction is a second order reaction.
C. The half-life period is independent of the concentration of X.
D. Decomposition of $\text{N}_2\text{O}_5$ is an example of the above reaction.
E. $\ln \frac{[R_o]}{[R]}$ vs time is valid for the above reaction.
Choose the correct answer from the options given below:
options: A, B, D and E Only
questions.explain:
The unit of the rate constant $k$ is $\text{L mol}^{-1}\text{ s}^{-1}$ (or $\text{M}^{-1}\text{ s}^{-1}$), which indicates that it is a second-order reaction. Thus, statement B is true.
For a second-order reaction, Rate = $k[X]^2$. If $[X]$ is increased $4$ times, Rate becomes $(4)^2 = 16$ times. Thus, statement A is true.
The half-life of a second-order reaction is $t_{1/2} = \frac{1}{k[X]_0}$, which depends on the initial concentration. Thus, statement C is false.
The decomposition of $\text{N}_2\text{O}_5$ is a well-known first-order reaction. Thus, statement D is false.
The equation $\ln \frac{[R_o]}{[R]} = kt$ is the integrated rate law for a first-order reaction. For second-order, it is $\frac{1}{[R]} - \frac{1}{[R_0]} = kt$. Thus, statement E is false.

questions.q:
Consider the following gas phase reaction being carried out in a closed vessel at $25^\circ\text{C}$.
$2A(g) \rightarrow 4B(g) + C(g)$
At time $30\text{ min}$, the total pressure of the system is $300\text{ mm Hg}$. At time $t = \infty$, the total pressure is $600\text{ mm Hg}$. The pressure of $C(g)$ at $30\text{ minutes}$ time interval would be _______ mm Hg.
questions.explain:
Let initial pressure of A be $P_0$.
At $t = \infty$, reactant A is completely consumed. 2 moles of A yield 5 moles of gaseous products (4B + 1C).
So, final pressure $P_\infty = \frac{5}{2} P_0 = 600 \implies P_0 = 240\text{ mm Hg}$.
At $t = 30\text{ min}$, let $2p$ be the drop in pressure of A.
$P_A = 240 - 2p$, $P_B = 4p$, $P_C = p$.
Total pressure $P_{total} = (240 - 2p) + 4p + p = 240 + 3p$.
Given $P_{total} = 300\text{ mm Hg}$ at $30\text{ min}$.
$240 + 3p = 300 \implies 3p = 60 \implies p = 20\text{ mm Hg}$.
Since $P_C = p$, the pressure of C at $30\text{ minutes}$ is $20\text{ mm Hg}$.
